title: Acts Chapter 17 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Acts chapter 17 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Acts Chapter 17 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Acts Chapter 17.

questions.question: In Acts 17, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: They came to Thessalonica where was a synagogue of the Jews
Paul reasoned with them for three sabbath days
Jews stirred up a riot in the city
Paul and Silas were sent to Berea by night
questions.correctAnswer: They came to Thessalonica where was a synagogue of the Jews
questions.explanation: Acts 17:1 states that they came to Thessalonica where was a synagogue of the Jews, which is the earliest event mentioned in the chapter.

questions.question: Which cities did Paul and his companions pass through before coming to Thessalonica?
questions.explanation: Acts 17:1 mentions that they passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia before coming to Thessalonica.

questions.question: How many sabbath days did Paul reason with the Jews in Thessalonica?
questions.explanation: Acts 17:2 states that Paul reasoned with them for three sabbath days.

questions.question: What did Paul open and allege to the Jews in Thessalonica?
options: That Christ must needs have suffered and risen again from the dead
That the law was no longer necessary
That the temple must be rebuilt
That the Messiah had not yet come
questions.correctAnswer: That Christ must needs have suffered and risen again from the dead
questions.explanation: Acts 17:3 says Paul opened and alleged that Christ must needs have suffered and risen again from the dead.

questions.question: Who believed Paul’s message in Thessalonica?
options: Some Jews, devout Greeks, and chief women
questions.correctAnswer: Some Jews, devout Greeks, and chief women
questions.explanation: Acts 17:4 states some Jews believed, and devout Greeks and chief women also believed.

questions.question: What did the unbelieving Jews do in Thessalonica out of envy?
options: They stirred up a city-wide uproar and assaulted Jason's house
They welcomed Paul and Silas warmly
They wrote letters to the governor of the province
questions.correctAnswer: They stirred up a city-wide uproar and assaulted Jason's house
questions.explanation: Acts 17:5 explains that unbelieving Jews moved with envy stirred up an uproar and assaulted Jason's house.

questions.question: Who was taken to the rulers of the city when Paul and Silas were not found?
questions.explanation: Acts 17:6 states that when Paul and Silas were not found, Jason and certain brethren were taken to the rulers.

questions.question: What accusation was made against Paul and Silas in Thessalonica?
options: They turn the world upside down and say there is another king, one Jesus
They were stealing from the temple
They were preaching rebellion against Rome openly
They were false teachers of the law
questions.correctAnswer: They turn the world upside down and say there is another king, one Jesus
questions.explanation: Acts 17:6-7 records the accusation that they had turned the world upside down and said there is another king, one Jesus.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the people and rulers when they heard the accusations against Paul and Silas?
options: They immediately imprisoned Paul and Silas
questions.explanation: Acts 17:8 says the people and rulers were troubled when they heard these things.

questions.question: What happened to Jason and the others after they gave security to the rulers?
questions.explanation: Acts 17:9 states that after taking security of Jason and others, they let them go.

questions.question: To which city were Paul and Silas immediately sent away by the brethren?
questions.explanation: Acts 17:10 states that the brethren sent Paul and Silas by night to Berea.

questions.question: The Bereans were more noble than those in Thessalonica because they received the word with readiness and searched the scriptures daily.
questions.explanation: Acts 17:11 describes the Bereans as more noble for receiving the word with readiness and searching the scriptures daily.

questions.question: Many Bereans believed, including honorable Greek women and men.
questions.explanation: Acts 17:12 confirms that many of them believed, including honorable Greek women and men.

questions.question: Paul was arrested by the city rulers in Thessalonica according to Acts 17.
questions.explanation: Acts 17 does not say Paul was arrested; Jason and certain brethren gave security and were let go (Acts 17:9).

questions.question: Paul and Silas stayed in Thessalonica for several months according to Acts 17.
questions.explanation: Acts 17 indicates they were sent away by night to Berea immediately (Acts 17:10), so they did not stay for several months.

medium.title: Acts Chapter 17 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Acts Chapter 17 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the Jews of Thessalonica do when they learned that Paul was preaching in Berea?
questions.explanation: Acts 17:13 states that the Jews of Thessalonica had knowledge that Paul was preaching at Berea and came there to stir up the people.

questions.question: What does Acts 17:14 promise will happen if someone does what verse 13 implies about stirring up the people?
options: They will be sent away for safety
questions.correctAnswer: They will be sent away for safety
questions.explanation: Acts 17:14 shows that because of the stirring up of the people, Paul was sent away to the sea for his safety.

questions.question: Where did the brethren send Paul after he was stirred up by the Jews from Thessalonica?
questions.explanation: Acts 17:15 indicates that the brethren conducted Paul to Athens.

questions.question: What did Paul notice about Athens while he waited there?
options: It was a city of many temples
It was wholly given to idolatry
questions.correctAnswer: It was wholly given to idolatry
questions.explanation: Acts 17:16 tells us that Paul's spirit was stirred when he saw that the city was given to idolatry.

questions.question: In Acts 17:17, where did Paul dispute daily with the Jews and devout persons?
questions.explanation: Acts 17:17 states that Paul disputed daily in the market with those he met.

questions.question: What did some philosophers say about Paul in Acts 17:18?
questions.explanation: Acts 17:18 records that certain philosophers called Paul a babbler because of his preaching about Jesus and the resurrection.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the Athenians to Paul's new doctrine?
options: They were curious and wanted to know more
questions.correctAnswer: They were curious and wanted to know more
questions.explanation: Acts 17:19 shows that the Athenians took Paul to the Areopagus to inquire about the new doctrine he was preaching.

questions.question: In Acts 17:20, what did the Athenians say about the things Paul was bringing to their ears?
questions.explanation: Acts 17:20 states that the Athenians found the things Paul brought to their ears to be strange.

questions.question: What does Acts 17:21 reveal about the interests of the Athenians?
options: They were only interested in trade
They spent time only on new things
They were indifferent to new ideas
questions.correctAnswer: They spent time only on new things
questions.explanation: Acts 17:21 indicates that the Athenians and strangers spent their time telling or hearing new things.

questions.question: What accusation does Paul make about the men of Athens in Acts 17:22?
questions.explanation: In Acts 17:22, Paul states that he perceives the men of Athens to be too superstitious.

questions.question: What inscription did Paul find on the altar in Athens according to Acts 17:23?
questions.explanation: Acts 17:23 mentions that Paul found an altar with the inscription 'TO THE UNKNOWN GOD.'

questions.question: What does Paul declare about the God who made the world in Acts 17:24?
options: He dwells in temples made with hands
He is Lord of heaven and earth
He is known only to the Jews
questions.correctAnswer: He is Lord of heaven and earth
questions.explanation: Acts 17:24 declares that God, who made the world, is the Lord of heaven and earth.

questions.question: True or False: Paul preached to both Jews and Gentiles in Athens.
questions.explanation: Acts 17:17 shows that Paul disputed in the synagogue with Jews and in the market with devout persons, indicating he preached to both.

questions.question: True or False: Paul was welcomed by all the Athenians without any opposition.
questions.explanation: Acts 17:18 shows that certain philosophers encountered Paul and questioned his teachings, indicating there was opposition.

questions.question: True or False: The Athenians were only interested in traditional teachings.
questions.explanation: Acts 17:21 states the Athenians spent their time on new things, showing their interest in new ideas.

hard.title: Acts Chapter 17 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Acts Chapter 17.

questions.question: According to Acts 17:25, what does God not require from men?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Acts 17:25 states that God is not worshipped with men's hands as though He needed anything.

questions.question: In Acts 17:26, what has God made of one blood?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because Acts 17:26 indicates that God made all nations of men from one blood.

questions.question: What does Acts 17:27 suggest we should do?
questions.explanation: Acts 17:27 encourages that they should seek the Lord and try to find Him.

questions.question: According to Acts 17:29, what should we not think the Godhead is like?
questions.explanation: Acts 17:29 warns that we ought not to think the Godhead is like gold, silver, or stone.

questions.question: What does Acts 17:30 say God commands all men to do?
questions.explanation: Acts 17:30 states that God now commands all men everywhere to repent.

questions.question: What did some people do when they heard of the resurrection of the dead in Acts 17:32?
questions.explanation: Acts 17:32 mentions that some mocked when they heard of the resurrection of the dead.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'kineo' in Acts 17:28 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Kineo' means 'to move' in Greek, as used in Acts 17:28 where it discusses movement in God.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used in Acts 17:28?
questions.explanation: Acts 17:28 contains a quotation from Greek poets, which is a form of literary technique.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to Acts 17:26 regarding God's creation of all nations?
questions.explanation: Genesis 1:27 refers to God creating mankind, which connects to Acts 17:26's theme of God making all nations.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to Acts 17:30 regarding God's command to repent?
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:17 echoes the call to repentance, connecting with the command in Acts 17:30.

questions.question: What precedes Acts 17:26 in the chapter?
questions.explanation: Acts 17:24 precedes Acts 17:26, discussing God's creation of the world and all things therein.

questions.question: What does Acts 17:31 tell us about the judgment of the world?
questions.explanation: Acts 17:31 states that God will judge the world by that man whom He has ordained, referring to Jesus.

questions.question: Acts 17:34 mentions certain individuals who believed. Which of the following is one of them?
questions.explanation: Acts 17:34 specifically names Dionysius the Areopagite as one who believed.

questions.question: True or False: Acts 17:30 indicates that God winks at times of ignorance.
questions.explanation: Acts 17:30 states that God winked at times of ignorance, showing His patience.

questions.question: True or False: Acts 17:32 suggests that everyone believed in the resurrection of the dead.
questions.explanation: Acts 17:32 indicates that some mocked the idea of the resurrection of the dead, showing disbelief.

theological.title: Acts Chapter 17 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Acts Chapter 17 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 17:3 teach about salvation?
options: Salvation is through Christ's suffering and resurrection
Salvation is earned by works of the law
Salvation is by following Jewish traditions
Salvation is attained through philosophical wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is through Christ's suffering and resurrection
questions.explanation: Acts 17:3 explains that Christ must suffer and rise from the dead and that Jesus is the Christ, indicating salvation is based on His redemptive work.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning God’s providence is taught in Acts 17:26?
options: God has predetermined the times and bounds of human habitation
God is indifferent to the affairs of nations
God’s providence is limited to spiritual matters only
God’s providence is based on human merit
questions.correctAnswer: God has predetermined the times and bounds of human habitation
questions.explanation: Acts 17:26 states God has determined the times before appointed and the bounds of their habitation, teaching divine sovereignty over history and geography.

questions.question: What doctrine about repentance is taught in Acts 17:30?
options: God commands all men everywhere to repent
Repentance is optional and culturally relative
Repentance is unnecessary due to ignorance
questions.correctAnswer: God commands all men everywhere to repent
questions.explanation: Acts 17:30 teaches that God now commands all people everywhere to repent, emphasizing the universal call to repentance.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 17:25 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Acts 17:25 states God is not served by human hands as if He needed anything, demonstrating God's self-sufficiency.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in Acts 17:27?
questions.explanation: Acts 17:27 explains God is not far from any one of us, indicating His omnipresence.

questions.question: How does the preaching of resurrection in Acts 17:31 connect to Old Testament prophecy?
options: It fulfills the prophetic assurance of a coming righteous judge
It contradicts the Old Testament hope of resurrection
It introduces a new doctrine unrelated to previous revelation
It rejects the concept of judgment entirely
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills the prophetic assurance of a coming righteous judge
questions.explanation: Acts 17:31 states God appointed a day to judge the world in righteousness by a man raised from the dead, connecting to prophetic themes of a coming righteous judge.

questions.question: In what way does Paul's speech in Acts 17:23-29 fulfill the Old Testament revelation of God?
options: By declaring the unknown God whom they ignorantly worship as the Creator God
By denying any knowledge of God’s existence
By equating God with idols made by human hands
By emphasizing human effort over divine revelation
questions.correctAnswer: By declaring the unknown God whom they ignorantly worship as the Creator God
questions.explanation: Acts 17:23-29 shows Paul identifying the altar to the unknown god with the true Creator God who made all things and is worshipped rightly.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 17:24 and 17:29 teach about God’s nature and human idolatry?
options: God is transcendent and not like graven images
God dwells in temples made by human hands
Human idols are true representations of God
God requires physical temples for worship
questions.correctAnswer: God is transcendent and not like graven images
questions.explanation: Acts 17:24 teaches God does not dwell in temples made with hands, and 17:29 teaches we should not think God is like gold, silver, or stone idols.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 17:28 and 17:30 teach about human existence and divine judgment?
options: Humans live in God and must repent because judgment is appointed
Human existence is independent of God and judgment is arbitrary
God is unknowable and judgment is impossible
Humans are God’s offspring but exempt from judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Humans live in God and must repent because judgment is appointed
questions.explanation: Acts 17:28 says we live and move in God, and 17:30 commands repentance because God has appointed a day of judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 17:11 and 17:12 teach about the reception of the gospel and evidence?
options: The Bereans examined Scriptures daily and many believed
Belief requires no examination of Scripture
The gospel is rejected by all without exception
Faith is blind and unrelated to evidence
questions.correctAnswer: The Bereans examined Scriptures daily and many believed
questions.explanation: Acts 17:11 shows Bereans searched the Scriptures daily, and 17:12 reports many believed, indicating faith grounded in scriptural examination.

questions.question: Sceptics claim the teaching in Acts 17:18–21 about new doctrines is simply philosophical babble without substance. What does Acts 17:18–21 actually teach?
options: Athenians were eager for new ideas and engaged Paul’s doctrine seriously
Paul’s teaching was universally rejected as nonsense
New doctrines were forbidden in the marketplace
questions.correctAnswer: Athenians were eager for new ideas and engaged Paul’s doctrine seriously
questions.explanation: Acts 17:21 states Athenians spent time telling or hearing new things, showing they were open and curious rather than dismissive.

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of Christ's kingship is taught in Acts 17:7?
options: Christ is declared as another king contrary to Caesar’s decrees
Christ is a political revolutionary seeking earthly power
Christ rejects all authority including divine
Christ’s kingship is purely symbolic without real authority
questions.correctAnswer: Christ is declared as another king contrary to Caesar’s decrees
questions.explanation: Acts 17:7 states that Paul and Silas say there is another king, one Jesus, which was considered contrary to Caesar’s decrees.

questions.question: What divine attribute is particularly demonstrated in Acts 17:31 regarding God’s judgment?
questions.explanation: Acts 17:31 states God will judge the world in righteousness, emphasizing His just and holy character.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning the role of Scripture is taught in Acts 17:2?
options: Paul reasons from the Scriptures to testify about Christ
Scriptures are irrelevant to the gospel message
Oral tradition is preferred over Scriptures
questions.correctAnswer: Paul reasons from the Scriptures to testify about Christ
questions.explanation: Acts 17:2 notes Paul reasoned three Sabbath days from Scriptures to demonstrate Jesus is Christ, showing the centrality of Scripture in evangelism.

questions.question: What theological significance does the conversion of Dionysius the Areopagite in Acts 17:34 hold?
options: It shows that even influential pagan philosophers can be converted by the gospel
It indicates that only common people accepted the gospel
It proves that conversion always leads to political power
It suggests conversion was coerced by threats
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that even influential pagan philosophers can be converted by the gospel
questions.explanation: Acts 17:34 mentions Dionysius the Areopagite, a member of the council, believed, showing the gospel’s power to reach elites.
